 Kalamazoo County sees record-breaking voter turnout in midterm elections
 By the time polls opened on the morning of Election Day, millions of Michigan voters had already cast their ballots. With absentee and early voting options, here’s how voters in Kalamazoo and greater Michigan participated in the Nov. 3 election. By Cori Osterman ● Election News ● November 19, 2026 
 A state operated Power BI dashboard visualized the different voting methods of Michigan voters. Source: Michigan Department of State Michigan Voting Dashboard . 
 The 126,838 Kalamazoo County voters who cast a ballot in the 2026 general election made history – participation exceeded every prior midterm election. That’s according to Kalamazoo County Clerk and Register of Deeds Meredith Place. Out of the county’s 188,508 active registered voters, 67.3% voted either absentee, early in-person, or on Election Day Nov. 3.
 The record turnout is on par with state and national rates so far. The state of Michigan has 7,431,143 voters with an “active” status in the Qualified Voter File. Of those active registered voters, 65% cast a ballot, according to the Michigan Department of State’s voting dashboard . Locally, the final counts were confirmed and announced Nov. 17 when the county’s Board of Canvassers completed their tally. The Board of State Canvassers will confirm its final counts by Nov. 23.
 Voter status remains active for registered voters unless a voter has no activity for a period of six consecutive years. The Michigan Department of State may also mark a voter as inactive if they move and do not respond to a cancellation notice.
 More people voted absentee and early in-person than on Election Day
 Kalamazoo County voters had three options for casting their ballots, according to the county’s election results:
 Election Day Voting: 58,639 voters (46.2%) voted in person at their assigned precincts on November 3.
 Absentee Voting: 51,120 voters (40.3%) cast absentee ballots.
 Early In-Person Voting: 17,079 voters (13.5%) voted during the nine-day early voting period preceding Election Day.
 Statewide, more than 35% of voters turned in a ballot before Election Day even began.
 Across county municipalities, the city of Kalamazoo had the highest number of Election Day votes with 13,982.
 While absentee voting accounted for most ballots cast before Election Day, Kalamazoo residents showed steady participation throughout the county’s early voting period. There were several days during early voting where Kalamazoo saw spikes in the number of ballots cast. Oct. 24, the first day of early voting accounted for 2,002 votes and Nov. 1, the final day to vote early, saw 2,709 votes.
 The canvass also settled a tie in the Village of Augusta Board of Trustees race. 
 Candidates Randy Padgett and Kelsey Kooiker both received 118 votes leaving the third seat in the race a tie. The canvassers determined the winner by placing two identical pieces of paper in a hat, one of which said “elected” and the other “not elected.” Padgett drew the “elected” slip and will serve as a trustee for the Village of Augusta.
 “It’s a pretty remarkable example of how close a local election can be, and a reminder that every single vote matters,” said County Clerk and Register of Deeds Meredith Place.
 The official results of every local and regional race in Kalamazoo County for the Nov. 3, 2026 general election is available here .
 Author
 Cori Osterman
 Cori Osterman (she/her) earned her master’s degree in communication from Western Michigan University in 2025, following her undergraduate degree in digital media journalism in 2024. During her junior year, Cori interned at WMUK, where she produced radio stories covering local and regional news. She was also involved with the Western Herald, WMU’s student-run newspaper, serving as a dedicated member for five years. She held multiple roles, including her two-year term as editor-in-chief. As a justice reporter, she continues her passion of uplifting voices through covering systems and issues in the Kalamazoo community.
